blocking.issue: The Zero-Downtime Upgrade row names Zero-downtime upgrades and hot reload as the owner of its bound, but states a different rule from that document. Zero-downtime upgrades uses shared Node-wide ceilings: the new process admits each ceiling minus the old process's usage, under a soft memory limit of 90% of the limit minus the old RSS, and the host keeps only the overlap extra free (about 0.6 GiB plus snapshots). The capacity document instead says both processes hold their full GOMEMLIMIT and doubles the host. It also offers a 90% split that halves each C_cap, which is not the owner's rule either. The design choice is still open as OQ-zero-downtime-upgrades-and-hot-reload-6, which this document owns and which blocks Planned (M1) in-place handover. The capacity document never mentions that question, so the two documents disagree and nothing decides between them.

non_blocking.suggestion: Line 268: "Its `AIModel` has one candidate, not `gemini` or `ollama`, so attempts = 1." AI/LLM gateway, Model routing, allows up to (`retries.attempts` + 1) × candidates attempts, and Routes with `ai.token-budget` allow 2 attempts (target). One candidate therefore gives attempts = 1 only if the Upstream sets no retries. Write: "one candidate and no `retries`, so attempts = 1".

Line 52 gives the hottest-key call bound as "min(offered, 2 × `requests`) per second", but Scalability, Distributed rate limits, states it per window: "2 × `requests` × N_serving / N_published calls per window". Write "min(offered, 2 × `requests` per `window`), as a per-second rate" so it does not overstate keys with windows longer than 1 s.

The Stream-bound row uses `ruralz_node_buffered_bytes` at 64 MiB as a stream-share signal. Observability defines that gauge as all buffered bytes "Of `limits.maxBufferedBytes`", and the stream share is 25% of that budget (Data plane, Streaming). Say that this proxy is stricter than Scalability's 50%-of-budget signal and can fire on non-stream buffering, and link OQ-capacity-planning-8's proposed `ruralz_node_stream_share_bytes`.

Rule 5 ("Enrollment MUST keep up with the largest scale-out step per egress address (K-18)") restates Deployment topologies, Enrollment per topology (line 468). Cite that section and OQ-deployment-topologies-15 (how rates are keyed behind shared egress) as the source, not K-18 alone.

Line 305 says the `ai.token-budget` default is `closed` citing ADR-0014. Pack 8.9 and section 10 add that the default is still subject to OQ-configuration-model-8. Append that Open question so the MUST on automatic failover is clearly conditional.

Line 426 applies the Divided pattern with "one Environment per Cell". Scalability, Regional versus global quotas, defines Divided as one Environment per Region. Say that the per-Cell use generalizes that pattern, or limit it to Cells in different Regions.

Line 61 sets interim values (10 MiB of audit per day for 365 days, a 1 GiB Raft log, 14 backups) with "until measured (hypothesis)" but no Open question. Point them at OQ-capacity-planning-3 or OQ-capacity-planning-9 so the path to measured values is explicit.
